extracted.intended_audience: university research offices and research institution staff preparing comments on federal proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting effective public comments on federal proposed rules, with a focus on issues and evidence relevant to research universities and their communities. Advice covers general comment-writing best practices and university-specific strategic points to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the Regulation Before Commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Most regulations have an introduction and background section where the agency lays out the purpose of the regulation and any applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the agency's introduction and background to grasp the regulation's purpose and legal context before submitting comments; this informs whether and how to engage on particular provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take a Clear Position
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state whether you agree with or disagree with the proposed rule (or an aspect of it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openly state your stance so agency reviewers can immediately understand your perspective and the comment's intent (supportive, opposed, or partially supportive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific and Detailed
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive, detailed comments (whether positive or negative) are most helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, specific points and reasoning rather than vague assertions; detail increases the usefulness of the comment to reviewers and increases likelihood of agency consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an Alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: If you disagree with a proposed action, suggest an alternative (including not regulating at all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explanation of how the alternative might meet the same objective or be more effective; offering practicable alternatives improves persuasiveness compared with only criticizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Your Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency reviewers look for sound science and reasoning in the comments they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back claims with evidence, data, citations, or logical analysis so reviewers can evaluate the basis of your assertions; scientific and technical justification is particularly important for research-related comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Specific Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the page number, column, and/or paragraph from the Federal Register if you are commenting on a particular word, phrase, or sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite exact locations in the Federal Register (page/column/paragraph) when addressing specific text to make it easy for agency staff to locate and consider your suggested edits or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan Ahead (Meet Deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period closes at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the date comments are due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track deadlines carefully and submit before the stated close time; last-minute submissions risk missing the deadline and being excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the Research Community Impacted
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the research community impacted (PIs, postdocs, students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which roles or groups within the research ecosystem will be affected so the agency understands the human and operational scope of the impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify Research Dollars Affected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimates (dollar amounts, budgets, grants affected) to convey the economic scale of the rule’s impact on research activity and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Compliance Burden Separate From Research Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Address compliance burden distinct from research mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate administrative/compliance costs and burdens from effects on the core research mission to clarify where the rule imposes operational vs. substantive research impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Specific Applicable Circulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific applicable circulars (Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200, Common Rule 45 CFR 46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant federal regulations and guidance documents by citation to demonstrate legal/regulatory grounding and to explain interactions or conflicts with existing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Research Integrity Considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the proposal might affect honesty, reproducibility, ethical conduct, oversight, or other integrity-related aspects of research practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Impacts on Specific Research Domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Address impacts on specific research domains (clinical trials, animal research, classified research, dual-use research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out domain-specific implications and operational constraints so agencies can assess differentiated effects across types of research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with Peer Institutions for Sign-on Letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with peer institutions for sign-on letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider collective action (joint letters or coordinated submissions) to demonstrate broader community agreement and strengthen visibility of shared concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Compliance Officer Implementation Perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide compliance officer perspective on implementation feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include practical input from institutional compliance or grants officers on how the rule would be implemented operationally and what feasibility or resource issues would arise.
